claim: The adult human brain receives 15–20% of cardiac output despite only representing 2% of body mass.
source: The adult human brain receives 15–20% of cardiac output despite only representing 2% of body mass (Bouma and Muizelaar, 1990; Satterthwaite et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bouma and Muizelaar, 1990 and Satterthwaite et al., 2014

claim: Infancy is characterized by fastest energy expenditure increase across lifespan.
source: Vast energy demand from the human brain starts from infancy, which is characterized by fastest energy expenditure increase across lifespan (Pontzer et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pontzer et al., 2021

claim: During infancy the brain size increases dramatically in parallel with rapid elaboration of new synapses, reaching 80–90% of lifetime maximum by age of year 2.
source: For example, during infancy the brain size increases dramatically in parallel with rapid elaboration of new synapses, reaching 80–90% of lifetime maximum by age of year 2 (Knickmeyer et al., 2008; Ouyang et al., 2019a; Pfefferbaum et al., 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Knickmeyer et al., 2008; Ouyang et al., 2019a; Pfefferbaum et al., 1994

claim: Functional networks in the human brain develop differentially following the order from primary sensorimotor to higher-order cognitive systems.
source: As a result of differential neuronal growth across cortex, functional networks in the human brain develop differentially following the order from primary sensorimotor to higher-order cognitive systems (Cao et al., 2017a; Huang and Vasung, 2014; Sidman and Rakic, 1982; Tau and Peterson, 2010; Yu et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2017a; Huang and Vasung, 2014; Sidman and Rakic, 1982; Tau and Peterson, 2010; Yu et al., 2016

claim: The default-mode network (DMN) is widely recognized as a fundamental neurobiological system associated with cognitive processes that are directed toward the self.
source: The default-mode network (DMN) (Raichle et al., 2001) is widely recognized as a fundamental neurobiological system associated with cognitive processes that are directed toward the self and has important implication in typical and atypical brain development (Buckner et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Raichle et al., 2001 and Buckner et al., 2008

claim: Primary sensorimotor (SM) and visual (Vis) networks emerge relatively earlier around and before birth.
source: Unlike primary sensorimotor (SM) and visual (Vis) networks emerging relatively earlier around and before birth (Cao et al., 2017b; Doria et al., 2010; Smyser et al., 2010), emergence of the vital resting-state DMN is not well established until late infancy (Gao et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao et al., 2017b; Doria et al., 2010; Smyser et al., 2010

claim: Emergence of the vital resting-state DMN is not well established until late infancy.
source: Unlike primary sensorimotor (SM) and visual (Vis) networks emerging relatively earlier around and before birth (Cao et al., 2017b; Doria et al., 2010; Smyser et al., 2010), emergence of the vital resting-state DMN is not well established until late infancy (Gao et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gao et al., 2009

claim: Regional brain metabolism, including glucose utilization and oxygen consumption, is closely coupled to regional CBF (rCBF) that delivers the glucose and oxygen needed to sustain metabolic needs.
source: Regional brain metabolism, including glucose utilization and oxygen consumption, is closely coupled to regional CBF (rCBF) that delivers the glucose and oxygen needed to sustain metabolic needs (Raichle et al., 2001; Vaishnavi et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Raichle et al., 2001; Vaishnavi et al., 2010

claim: Infant rCBF has been conventionally measured with positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT).
source: Infant rCBF has been conventionally measured with positron emission tomography (PET) (Altman et al., 1988; Altman et al., 1993; Chugani and Phelps, 1986; Chugani et al., 1987) and single-photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT) (Chiron et al., 1992), which are not applicable to infants due to the associated exposure to radioactive tracers.
evidence: Supported by citations to Altman et al., 1988; Altman et al., 1993; Chugani and Phelps, 1986; Chugani et al., 1987; Chiron et al., 1992

claim: PET and SPECT are not applicable to infants due to the associated exposure to radioactive tracers.

evidence: Based on knowledge that radioactive tracers are harmful to infants

claim: ASL is especially suitable for rCBF measurements of infants.

claim: RCBF in the DMN (67.8 ± 2.08 ml/100 g/min) regions was in the middle (all ts (47) > 2.87, p<0.05, FDR corrected).

claim: Significant correlations (p<0.001) were found between rCBF and FC in both 0-12 months and 12-24 months age groups.
source: To test the hypothesis that rCBF increases in the DMN regions underlie emergence of this vital functional network, correlation between rCBF and FC was conducted across randomly selected voxels within the DMN of all infants aged 0–12 months (Figure 4a) and all infants aged 12–24 months (Figure 4b). Significant correlations (p<0.001) were found in both age groups.
evidence: Demonstrated by correlation analysis results shown in Figure 4a and 4b

claim: Partial correlation analysis between rCBF and FC after regressing out age effects confirmed significant correlation between rCBF and FC in the DMN regions in both 0–12-month (p<0.001) and 12–24-month (p<0.001) groups excluding the age effect.
source: Partial correlation analysis between rCBF and FC after regressing out age effects also confirmed significant correlation between rCBF and FC in the DMN regions in both 0–12-month (p<0.001) and 12–24-month (p<0.001) groups excluding the age effect.
evidence: Demonstrated by partial correlation statistical analysis

claim: Most of the significant correlations (r > rcrit) between the DMN FC and voxel-wise rCBF were found in the voxels in the DMN regions, such as PCC, IPL, and LTC, but not in the Vis or SM regions.

claim: Correlation between the SM FC and rCBF across the brain showed percent of voxels with significant correlation was close to zero.

claim: The coupling of rCBF and FC is specific in the DMN regions, not in the primary sensorimotor (Vis or SM) regions.
source: Second, a nonparametric permutation analysis without a prior hypothesis at the voxel level across the whole brain was conducted to confirm the coupling of rCBF and FC is specific in the DMN regions (Figure 5), not in the primary sensorimotor (Vis or SM) regions (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), demonstrating the robustness of the results on physiological underpinning of functional network emergence in the DMN.
evidence: Demonstrated by nonparametric permutation analysis results shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2
